units.translation: Μᾶτερ, ἅ μ᾽ ἔτικτες ἀλαοῖσι καὶ δεδορκόσιν [Mother, you who bore me to the blind and the seeing]
Ποιναῖς τε τίνειν τῆσδ᾽ αἰκίας [and to pay penalties for this outrage]
Thus from the apograph, corrected to ποινάς [penalties].
Ποιναῖς δὲ ποίων [with penalties of what kind]
Ἔκτεινα τὴν τεκοῦσαν ἀντικτόνοις [I killed the mother with murder in return]
Μηδὲ πιοῦσα κόνις μέλαν αἷμα πολιτᾶν δι᾽ ὀργὰν [nor may the dust drink the black blood of citizens through wrath]
Λέξωμεν ἐπ᾿ Ἀργείοις εὐχὰς ἀγαθὰς ἀγαθῶν [Let us utter prayers for the Argives, good things for good men]
I pay with penalties for sins
he repaid me with these penalties
I thought I would be wasted away by such penalties
I say that someone is plotting with penalties
to send with penalties for the father
with penalties for the dearest father
to snatch away the murderous penalties of ruin from the city
Mother, you who bore me to the blind and the seeing
and to pay penalties for this outrage
Thus from the apograph, corrected to penalties
I killed the mother with murder in return
nor may the dust drink the black blood of citizens through wrath
Let us utter prayers for the Argives, good things for good men
Θυσίαι πα-τρὸς πολυκανεῖς βοτῶν [Sacrifices of the father, rich in cattle]
Ἐν ποιονόμοις ματρὸς ἀρχαίας [In the grassy places of the ancient mother]
Sacrifices of the father, rich in cattle
In the grassy places of the ancient mother
Ποιναῖς δὲ ποίων [with penalties of what kind]
Ποῖον δ᾽ ἀμείψεσθε γαίας πέδον τᾶσδ᾽ [What land will you exchange for this ground?]
Ποίῳ μόρῳ δὲ τούσδε φὴς [By what fate do you say these men...]
Ποίου χρόνου δὲ καὶ [And of what time...]
Ποίαν Ἐρινὺν τήνδε δώμασιν [What Erinys is this upon the house?]
Ποίοισι βωμοῖς χρώμενος τοῖς δημίοις? ποία δὲ χέρνιψ φρατέρων [Using what altars of the people? And what lustral water of the clansmen?]
Ἐκ ποίου φρονήματος ἀνδρῶν Πε-λασγῶν τήνδ᾽ ἀτιμάζεις [With what thought of Pelasgian men do you dishonor this woman?]

where I changed ποίου [of what kind], introduced from a gloss, to τίνος [of whom] on the conjecture of an anonymous scholar. For it is not credible that Aeschylus preferred to shorten the diphthong rather than say τίνος [of whom].
Ποίοισιν εἰπὼν προξένοις [Having said with what patrons]
Ποία ξυνωρὶς τῆσδε [What pair of this woman]
Γέγων᾽ ἡμῖν λόγον, ποίῳ λαβών σε Ζεὺς ἐπ᾿ αἰτιάματι — [Tell us the story, with what charge did Zeus take you —]
Καὶ σὸν διδάξω πατέρα [And I will teach your father]
from the apograph for τοῖα [such things]
do you bid to raise a shout?
to what misfortune shall I liken it?
do you mean the shepherd of sheep?
having found what remedy for this disease?
What land will you exchange for this ground?
By what fate do you say these men...
What Erinys is this upon the house?
Using what altars of the people? And what lustral water of the clansmen?
